chapter: Childhood and first music in Oklahoma
title: Boley training school: the trumpet he wanted, the clarinet he got
summary: Bandmaster George Buford taught him fingering but put him on clarinet; he learned it and became the better of two clarinettists before leaving Boley.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: In Sapulpa, yeah. So he went and put me in a training school down in Boley, Oklahoma.
Yeah. And they had a music teacher there. He taught me how to finger the trumpet.
What had you been playing before the trumpet?
Oh, I just liked music. I wasn't playing anything.
Oh, you hadn't tried anything then.
I hadn't tried any instrument at all.
So the trumpet was your first...

Yeah. Well, I had heard Louis Armstrong, you know, and I figured, 'Well, hell, that's what I want to play. I want to be like Pops,' you know. But when they got the instruments for the school band, the cat, George Buford, who was my music teacher, he had taught me the scale on the trumpet...

George Buford. He had taught me how to play the scale on his trumpet, you know. So I figured he was going to put me on trumpet because I knew the scale, you know. And boy, I was so disappointed, and I was mad like a wet hen. I called him everything under the sun -- underneath my breath, of course. But he put me... He started me out on clarinet, you know. And that made me... You know, that kind of threw me a curve, because I wasn't expecting to play clarinet. I loved trumpet.
But I went on and learned it anyway, you know, because he said, 'Well, either you play this or you don't play.' So

he knew that I wanted to play, so he just... He shoved me right into it. But I'm glad he did, because at that time, I didn't know nothin'. I didn't know that the clarinet played twice as fast as the trumpet. I didn't have the slightest idea about that, you know. So I'd say, 'Well, okay, if that's what I have to do, this is what I have to do.' So I learned to play the clarinet.

After that, after I really got good on the clarinet, I liked it. I liked the instrument. They had two of us playing clarinet, a guy named Marlin(?) and myself. And I was the best clarinettist out of the two of us. So I figured it was time for me to move and, you know, get to know music. So I decided to split, which I did. I cut out and went to...
